packageRules.description: Consumer-side `ci.yml`, rendered by THIS layer from `ci.yml.tera` with `when = "always"`. Action bumps happen upstream in pj-deno and flow down via `kata apply`, so a Renovate-driven local bump is reverted on the next apply and re-opened forever. The canonical pins live in `.kata/vars.toml`, which pj-base's customManager scans. Owned here rather than in pj-base because pj-base cannot know a deno layer composes above it — and because `ci.yml` is a name any project may legitimately hand-write.

`actions.deno_setup` is kata-managed in consumer repos: pj-deno back-fills it into `.kata/vars.toml` with `merge-toml, when = "always"` so that a project adopting this layer late (`kata add`, where the `once` seed is skipped) still gets the pin. That back-fill means a consumer-side bump is reverted on the next apply, re-opened by Renovate, and so on forever. The canonical bump therefore happens upstream in pj-deno's own `vars.deno.toml` — which pj-base's customManager scans via its `vars.<layer>.toml` pattern — and flows down to every consumer on the next `kata apply`. Scoped to `.kata/vars.toml` so pj-deno's own seed file is still scanned. Same ownership model as pj-base's `anthropics/claude-code-action` rule.
